transcripts.caption: Hey Stewie, Peter here, and I'm going to teach you the fundamentals of calculus!
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: Calculus has a lot of rules and formulas, but my goal is for you to come away feeling like you could've invented calculus yourself, covering core ideas in a visual way.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: We'll start with the area of a circle: pi times its radius squared.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: Well, we can imagine slicing the circle into many concentric rings.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: If we straighten out each ring, we get a rectangle whose width is the circumference, 2πr, and whose thickness is a tiny difference in radius, dr.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: The area of each little rectangle is 2πr times dr.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: When we stack all these rectangles, they form a triangle under the graph of 2πr.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: The area of that triangle is ½ * base * height, which works out to pi times the radius squared!
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: Wow! So what does that have to do with calculus, Peter?
transcripts.speaker: STEWIE

transcripts.caption: By slicing the circle into thinner and thinner rings, our approximation gets more and more accurate, approaching the true area.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: This process of summing many small quantities to find a total is called integration, which is one of the big ideas in calculus.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: Another big idea is the derivative, which is how sensitive a function is to small changes in its input.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: It turns out that finding the derivative is the inverse of finding an integral, and that's the fundamental theorem of calculus!
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: This means that if you know how a function changes, you can reverse engineer what the function must be.
transcripts.speaker: PETER

transcripts.caption: You could've invented calculus yourself, Stewie!
transcripts.speaker: PETER
